subject: Pilot: multi-index federation — AtlasData pilot proposal
messages:
From: Sara Holmes <sara@atlasdata.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: multi-index federation — AtlasData pilot proposal

Hi Neha —

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. AtlasData is excited to propose a short pilot to validate a multi-index federation strategy for customers that need high-recall search across mixed backends (Pinecone + pgvector + S3-backed dense indexes).

High-level ask: a 6-week tech pilot to prove query routing, failover, and snapshot sync between hot vector stores (Pinecone) and cold S3-backed pgvector indexes. Goals:
- Validate routing policy latency targets (p95 <= 200ms for hot-path queries)
- Proof of consistent top-k recall across store boundaries for our 10k test queries
- Demonstrate safe snapshotting and rehydration from S3 for restore workflows

We put together a short outline attached (atlas-pilot-outline.pdf) with scope, roles, and a proposed timeline. For the commercial side we propose a nominal co-funded engineering commitment and will share an SoW draft if you like the technical scope.

Open items we want to confirm upfront:
1) Which Redwood model(s) and quantization profile will you recommend for the hot-path in Dedicated or Hosted?
2) Any constraints on credentials/keys for S3 snapshot access in a Private deployment?
3) Can we pull in Pinecone for a short sync call to confirm replication semantics? (cc: Mike Chen from Pinecone)

Would love to schedule a 30m sync this week to align.

Best,
Sara Holmes
Head of Partnerships, AtlasData

Attachment: atlas-pilot-outline.pdf (1 page)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holmes <sara@atlasdata.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: multi-index federation — AtlasData pilot proposal

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the outline and for proposing a concrete scope. This looks promising and aligned with the types of partner pilots we want to standardize. A couple quick notes and asks before we lock the kickoff:

Technical clarifications
- Hot-path model: for this pilot we recommend starting with a mid-sized open model we already support in Hosted to keep latency predictable (we'll propose a few models in the tech sync). If the workload needs Dedicated, we can detail throughput targets in the SoW.
- S3 access: for Private customers we typically require pre-provisioned role-based credentials or a short-lived presigned flow. We can accommodate either, but will need an S3 bucket policy stub for the SOC review.

Operational asks
- Can you include an explicit acceptance criteria table in the SoW (recall thresholds, latency SLOs, and export/import window limits)?
- Please flag any customer PII/data residency requirements up front.

Commercial and scheduling
- Ben, Laura: can you confirm whether we want to propose co-funding engineering hours or trade credits for the pilot?
- Sara: I can do a 30m technical sync Tuesday 10/6 between 10–11am PT or Wednesday 10/7 after 1pm PT. Which works best?

If you want, go ahead and attach a SoW draft and we'll do a light redline.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference
From: Sara Holmes <sara@atlasdata.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mike Chen <mike@pinecone.io>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: multi-index federation — AtlasData pilot proposal

Hi Neha, Ben —

Thanks for the quick reply and clear asks. Attaching a first-pass SoW (atlas-pilot-sow-draft.docx) and a short test dataset description. Quick answers inline:

- Acceptance criteria: included in the SoW draft (section 2.1) — we suggest recall >= 0.92 for top-20 and p95 latency <= 250ms for combined routing. Happy to tighten with your input.
- S3: we can provide an IAM role with scoped Get/Put/List for the test bucket for the pilot timeline. If Redwood prefers presigned URLs that's also fine.
- Data residency: this initial pilot targets non-PII public datasets; if a customer requires EU residency we'll run a separate regional pilot.

Mike — joining here to confirm Pinecone is comfortable with a temporary replication flow for the pilot and to sync on vector fidelity expectations.

Proposed: Tuesday 10/6 10:30am PT for a 30m tech sync. If that works we'll send a calendar invite and a pre-kick checklist.

Regards,
Sara Holmes
Head of Partnerships, AtlasData

Attachments: atlas-pilot-sow-draft.docx (3 pages), atlas-testset-specs.csv (inline link)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sara Holmes <sara@atlasdata.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mike Chen <mike@pinecone.io>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: multi-index federation — AtlasData pilot proposal

All — happy to move forward. Quick commercial position: Redwood can commit an initial 40 engineering hours as co-funding for the 6-week pilot, with additional hours scoped as change requests. We prefer a trial credit arrangement rather than discounted professional services for simplicity.

Pre-kick checklist (attached: interop-prekick-checklist.xlsx) — please review before the sync:
- Confirm S3 bucket ARN and chosen access method (IAM role vs presigned)
- Provide sample of 1k documents and embedding vector spec (model name + quantization)
- Confirm Pinecone index schema and replication window
- Confirm a single Redwood contact for day-to-day triage (Neha to be the primary)

Neha — I flagged the SoW and will send a short commercial term sheet after your review. Sara — 10/6 10:30am PT works for us. Sending calendar moment and pre-kick doc now.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
